title: Concentrated poverty, ambient air pollution, and child cognitive development
summary: In a national infant cohort, random-forest mediation models estimated that about one-third of the association between neighborhood poverty and age-four cognitive scores was statistically mediated by air-quality disparities. This observational analysis does not establish that pollution caused the cognitive differences.
ai_technology: Supervised random forests within causal mediation estimated pollutant-specific mediation of poverty-associated cognitive differences.
organization: University of Southern California; University of California, Berkeley; University of Washington

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: The study matched a national infant cohort to more than 50 pollutants and performed mediation and sensitivity analyses using supervised random forests.
evidence.unknown: Observational mediation estimates rely on measured covariates and do not prove causal effects of poverty or pollutants.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised random forests within causal mediation estimated pollutant-specific mediation of poverty-associated cognitive differences.
